$$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{(\frac{2-x}{3})} \\ y & =\frac{3}{x-2}\end{aligned}

Finally, since $t\ne 0$ and $x=-3t+2$ , we must have $x\ne 2.$

$$
y=\frac{3}{x-2},\,x\ne 2.
